facts.fact: Adwave says TV advertising for an e-commerce business starts at $30 a day.
facts.quote: TV advertising for your e-commerce business starts at just $30 a day with Adwave.

facts.fact: Adwave suggests testing budgets of $2,000-5,000 to gauge TV response before committing larger investment.
facts.quote: Testing budgets of $2,000-5,000 let you gauge TV response before committing larger investment.

facts.fact: Adwave suggests scaling e-commerce TV budgets of $10,000-50,000 monthly to build meaningful brand awareness.
facts.quote: Scaling budgets of $10,000-50,000 monthly build meaningful brand awareness.

facts.fact: Major brands spend hundreds of thousands of dollars monthly on TV advertising, according to the Adwave guide.
facts.quote: Major brands spend hundreds of thousands monthly, but meaningful results are achievable at much lower levels.

facts.fact: The guide uses an average CPM of $25 as its example assumption for TV pricing.
facts.quote: At an average CPM of $25, $10,000 monthly delivers approximately 400,000 ad views nationally.

facts.fact: Adwave states it creates a commercial for free, and the guide says professional e-commerce commercial production costs that would otherwise be $20,000-100,000 disappear.
facts.quote: Production costs that might have been $20,000-100,000 for a professional e-commerce commercial disappear entirely.

facts.fact: Adwave says its TV ads run on more than 100 premium channels during prime viewing hours.
facts.quote: Your ad runs on [100+ premium channels](https://adwave.com/channels/) during prime viewing hours.

facts.fact: The guide advises evaluating e-commerce TV advertising over 60-90 day windows rather than weekly.
facts.quote: Evaluate TV over 60-90 day windows, not weekly.

facts.fact: The guide describes the holiday season as running from November to December and as the peak e-commerce period.
facts.quote: Holiday season (November-December) represents the peak e-commerce period.

facts.fact: The guide says post-holiday campaigns can drive January and February sales, when customer acquisition costs often decline and competition decreases.
facts.quote: Post-holiday campaigns can drive January and February sales when customer acquisition costs often decline and competition decreases.

facts.fact: AdWave states that brands doing $1 million or more in annual revenue with positive unit economics are typically ready to test TV advertising.
facts.quote: Brands doing $1 million or more in annual revenue with positive unit economics are typically ready to test TV.
